newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bureaucrats to hold Friday 13th strike.
newsitem.headline: Australian bureaucrats to hold Friday 13th strike.

text.p: Thousands of Australian bureaucrats will mark Friday the 13th with a 13-minute strike against government cutbacks.
The main public sector trade union said on Thursday its members would hold the symbolic 'black Friday' stoppage by turning off their computers and not answering phones or conducting any business.

"Our members will be dressed in black in a gesture of mourning for what Australia will lose if the Howard government continues to 'slash and burn' public sector services and jobs," said Wendy Caird, national secretary of the Commonwealth and Public Sector Union.
Prime Minister John Howard's coalition government announced in its last budget in May that it was cutting 16,000 civil service jobs after slashing thousands in its previous budget.
Caird said it had also implemented a series of other reforms opening the way "for hand-picked department heads to gain massive pay increases".
Caird's union represents 60,000 of Australia's 130,000 national civil servants.
